subject.title: Sunol Glen Unified School District — Measure K (GO Bond Measure)

text: To improve the quality of local education; complete the Main Building retrofit and renovation; replace deteriorating plumbing, electrical, sewer, heating and ventilation systems; and modernize and upgrade old classrooms and restrooms; shall Sunol Glen Unified School District’s measure be adopted authorizing $6,100,000 of bonds at legal rates, generating on average $431,700 annually while bonds are outstanding at approximate rates of $35 per $100,000 assessed value, with audits, citizens’ oversight, no money for salaries and funds staying local?

analysis.title: Impartial Analysis
analysis.by: Andrea L. Weddle, Interim County Counsel The above statement is an impartial analysis of Measure K, which is printed in full in this sample ballot pamphlet. If you desire an additional copy of the measure, please call the Elections Official’s office at (510) 272-6933 and a copy will be mailed at no cost to you. You may also access the full text of the measure on the Alameda County website at the following address: www.acvote.org.

text:
ANALYSIS BY THE COUNTY COUNSEL FOR THE COUNTY OF ALAMEDA OF A SUNOL GLEN UNIFIED SCHOOL DISTRICT BOND MEASURE Measure K (“Measure”) seeks voter approval to authorize the Sunol Glen Unified School District (“District”) to issue and sell bonds of up to $6,100,000 in aggregate principal amount at interest rates within the legal limits. If 55% of those who vote on the Measure vote “yes,” the District will be authorized to issue bonds in the amount noted above. Approval of this Measure will authorize a levy on the assessed value of taxable property within the District by an amount needed to pay the principal and interest on these bonds in each year that the bonds are outstanding. The District’s best estimate of the average annual tax rate necessary to fund the bond issue is $33.54 per $100,000 of the assessed valuation of a taxed property. The final fiscal year in which the tax is anticipated to be collected at the estimated average rate is 2058-59. The District’s best estimate of the highest tax is $35.00 per $100,000 of assessed valuation of a taxed property. The final fiscal year anticipated to collect the tax at the estimated highest rate is 2056-57. The District’s best estimate of total debt service to repay the bonds (including principal and interest) is approximately $13,815,000. The District estimates the tax would generate on average approximately $431,700 annually while bonds are outstanding.
California Education Code Section 15100 restricts the use of proceeds from bond sales to items such as building school buildings, improving school grounds, and supplying school buildings and grounds with equipment. Proceeds may only be used for the projects listed in the Measure and not for any other purpose, such as teacher and administrator salaries.
This Measure provides that the bond proceeds will fund authorized projects, which are generally described in the District’s 2026 Five Year Facilities Master Plan and the full text of the Measure printed in the voter information guide, examples of which include, among others: the Main Building retrofit and renovation; replacing building systems such as plumbing, electrical, sewer, heating and ventilation; and upgrading classrooms and restrooms.
The Measure includes a required disclosure that approval of the Measure does not guarantee completion of all projects, some of which might require funding from the State that is subject to appropriation by the Legislature. Certain accountability measures apply, such as establishing a separate account to deposit the proceeds from the sale of the bonds. To ensure that the proceeds are spent only for the types of projects listed in the Measure, it provides for an independent citizens’ oversight committee, an annual performance audit, an annual financial audit, and an annual report by the District’s chief fiscal officer to the District’s governing board, stating the amount of bond proceeds received and expended and the status of any project funded from the proceeds.
This Measure is placed on the ballot by the governing board of the District.
Tax Rate Statement Of Bond Measure K
Tax Rate Statement Regarding Proposed Sunol Glen Unified School District General Obligation Bonds

An election will be held in the Sunol Glen Unified School District (the “District”) of Alameda County, California, on November 3, 2026, to authorize the sale of up to $6,100,000 in bonds of the District to finance school facility improvements as described in the measure. If such bonds are authorized and sold, principal and interest on the bonds will be payable only from the proceeds of

property tax levies made upon the taxable property in the District. The following information is provided in compliance with Sections 9400-9404 of the Elections Code of the State of California. Such information is based upon the best estimates and projections presently available from official sources, upon experience within the District, and other demonstrable factors.
Based upon the foregoing and projections of the District’s assessed valuation, the following information is provided: 1. The best estimate of the average annual tax rate which would be required to be levied to fund this bond issue over the entire duration of the bond debt service, based on a projection of assessed valuations available at the time of filing of this statement, is $33.54 per $100,000 of assessed value. The final fiscal year in which the tax is anticipated to be collected is 2058-59. 2. The best estimate of the highest tax rate which would be required to be levied to fund this bond issue, based on a projection of assessed valuations available at the time of filing of this statement, is $35.00 per $100,000 of assessed value. It is estimated that such rate would be levied in fiscal years 2027-28 through 2056-57. 3. The best estimate of the total debt service, including the principal and interest, that would be required to be repaid if all the bonds are issued and sold is approximately $13,815,000. Voters should note the estimated tax rate is based on the assessed value (not market value) of taxable property on the Alameda County’s official tax rolls. Property owners should consult their own property tax bills and tax advisors to determine their property’s assessed value and any applicable tax exemptions.
The attention of all voters is directed to the fact that the foregoing information is based upon projections and estimates only, which amounts are not maximum amounts and are not binding upon the District. The actual debt service, tax rates and the years in which they will apply may vary from those used to provide the estimates set forth above, due to factors such as variations in the timing of bond sales, the par amount of bonds sold and market interest rates available at the time of each sale, actual assessed valuations over the term of the bonds, and other factors. The date and amount of bonds sold at any given time will be determined by the District based on the need for project funds and other considerations. The actual interest rates at which the bonds will be sold will depend on conditions in the bond market at the time of sale. Actual future assessed valuations will depend upon the amount and value of taxable property within the District as determined by the County Assessor in the annual assessment and the equalization process.

s SHAY GALLETTI/ 
Superintendent, Sunol Glen Unified School District

strong: Vote Yes on Measure “K”! Let’s protect our investment
and finish improving Sunol Glen School!

text:
Sunol Glen School is the center of our community. Our school has served our community for over 100 years, maintaining high academic standards within a positive and nurturing learning environment. It has also built strong community partnerships. For this reason, many generations of families continue to be part of our rich academic and cultural experience. However, while our teachers and staff focus on student success, our aging facilities remain a challenge.
Faced with deteriorating facilities, our community approved a school improvement funding measure in 2022 to renovate our historic Main Building. Built in 1925, the Building required major seismic retrofitting, including removing hazardous materials. Although many critical repairs were completed, and funds stretched as far as possible, additional needs remain today.
: Requires final phases of structural and infrastructure repairs, including window and door replacements, electrical, fencing, site work, and classroom upgrades.
: Modernize and renovate our learning environments to ensure they meet today’s safety and quality standards.
– Address critical items such as roofs, electrical and HVAC systems, playgrounds, safety and security improvements.
: Tax rates are estimated to remain amongst the lowest compared to area school districts.
Dollars stay local, benefiting our entire community.

By law, funds may be spent only on voter-approved projects and will be audited annually with independent citizen oversight. Without this investment, aging facilities will continue to deteriorate, resulting in costly emergency repairs in the future. Measure “K” ensures we have a safe and quality learning environment for generations to come.

strong: Join us in VOTING YES ON MEASURE K!
